newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares recover ground on Rao news.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares recover ground on Rao news.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi bourse closed marginally higher as speculators made some purchases following news of former prime minister Narasimha Rao winning a temporary reprieve in a criminal forgery case, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 0.42 points higher at 683.62.

"The market regained strength and speculators turned active enthused by reports that former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao got anticipatory bail till October 14," said S. Juneja of brokers Juneja Associates.
Delhi High Court Judge S.K. Mahajan granted Rao pre-emptive, or anticipatory, bail until a lower court holds a hearing into the seven-year-old case next Monday.

Judge Mahajan said Rao could apply for ordinary bail at the October 14 session, when he was scheduled to be formally charged with forgery and two other counts carrying a maximum sentence of seven years in jail.
If denied bail, Rao would be put in custody pending trial.
Reliance Industries gained 1.80 rupees to 189.80 on speculative buying, brokers said.
TISCO gained 1.10 rupees to 165.60, while State Bank of India gained 2.25 rupees to close at 212.35.
ACC gained 30 rupees to close at 1,680 on selective institutional buying, brokers said.
